name: NJ-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 5-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Mejia's incumbency and large fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
No public polling, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: a D+5 seat, an incumbent who has outraised Hathaway roughly three-to-one, and no outside spending against Mejia. Markets at 95% for the Democrat confirm the picture, so the forecast stays near the baseline with only a small trim for the thin cash-on-hand figures and absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Hathaway closing, or a surge of Republican outside spending, would be the first sign this is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NJ-11 leans Democratic by about five points, and first-term incumbent Analilia Mejia is seeking another term. She has raised about $1.8 million to Joe Hathaway's roughly $660,000, and outside groups have spent only in her support. Hathaway ends with little cash on hand, limiting his ability to close the gap late.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 95%. With a favorable environment for Democrats layered on the district's lean, Mejia is a clear favorite, though the lack of polling keeps some uncertainty in the estimate.
